主要内容: On February 2, 2012, the U.S. Treasury and Labor Departments announced two executive actions aimed at enhancing retirement security for American workers. These measures focus on increasing transparency in the 401(k) plan marketplace and expanding retirement plan options to help individuals save responsibly and securely. The Treasury Department’s proposal seeks to reduce regulatory burdens and provide retirees with flexible 'lifetime income' options, allowing them to receive benefits as a stream of income for as long as they live. This can offer greater certainty and reduce the risk of outliving retirement savings. Treasury Secretary Tim Geithner emphasized the importance of providing sensible, accessible choices for managing retirement savings. Meanwhile, the Department of Labor issued a final rule requiring employers to disclose administrative and investment costs associated with pension and 401(k) plans, with a three-month extension to the effective date, meaning compliance is due by July 1, 2012. Secretary of Labor Hilda L. Solis highlighted the significance of transparency in retirement plans, stating that better information on fees and expenses will enable informed decisions and cost savings. Together, these actions aim to expand retirement options and improve transparency, helping working families plan for retirement and manage their savings effectively. The U.S. Treasury and Labor Departments have introduced new guidance to enhance retirement security by focusing on both the accumulation of savings and the use of those savings for retirement income. The guidance includes three key proposals: 1. Encouraging partial annuity options to allow retirees to receive a steady income stream while keeping some savings invested. 2. Removing regulatory barriers to longevity annuities, enabling retirees to purchase guaranteed income starting at an advanced age. 3. Clarifying rules for plan rollovers and spousal protection to facilitate flexible retirement options. These changes aim to provide retirees with more choices and better financial security. Additional details are available on Treasury.gov and Regulations.gov.
